title: Validator
description: x-validator validates the fields inside its host (usually a <form>): each field's validate rules are checked when the host's validateOn events fire (blur by default), a failing field gets aria-invalid, the errorClass and an error message after it, and a <form> host refuses to submit until every field passes, focusing the first invalid field and firing wb:validator:validate. Rules: required, email, url, number, integer, min:N, max:N, minLength:N, maxLength:N, pattern:REGEX, match:NAME.

validateOn.description: Which events on the fields re-check the field that fired them, space-separated: any of blur, change, input. A <form> host always checks every field on submit.
validateOn.visualReason: Changes when a field is checked, not how anything looks until it is (#1844).

showErrors.description: Show the first failing rule's message in a span.x-validator__error right after the field. Set showErrors="false" to mark the field (aria-invalid, errorClass) without a message.
showErrors.visualReason: Only a field that has failed a check shows its message (#1844).

errorClass.description: Class put on a field that fails its rules (and taken off when it passes). The default is styled in validator.css with the danger border colour.
errorClass.visualReason: Only a field that has failed a check carries it (#1844).

successClass.description: Class put on a field that passes its rules once checked (and taken off when it fails). The default is styled in validator.css with the success border colour.
successClass.visualReason: Only a field that has been checked carries it (#1844).

validate.description: Set on each field, not on the host: its rules, space-separated, e.g. `required email` or `minLength:8`.

wb:validator:validate.description: Fired after the whole form is validated, on submit or validate().

setup: <form x-validator validateOn="input" showErrors="false"><input name="user" validate="required minLength:3"><button>Send</button></form>
